Kaunas Slobodca Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kauno apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Vilijampolė, known as Slobodka, developed as a distinct Jewish community from the second half of the 17th century, with close ties to Kėdainiai, documented elsewhere in this collection, from which its first settlers likely came; it offered refuge to Kaunas's Jews during several expulsions. The Great Synagogue, built in 1772, was funded by Rabbi Moshe Soloveichik, an influential lobbyist and the synagogue's first rabbi. About 600 Jewish families lived in Slobodka by 1824, reaching 2,973 individuals by 1847. Its most famous yeshiva, Knesset Israel, established in 1882, became an important center of the Musar movement and one of the most influential Orthodox yeshivot in the world. Incorporated into Kaunas in 1919, Slobodka held about 10,000 Jews by 1940; after the 1941 German invasion, it became the main site of the Kaunas Ghetto, which held 29,760 Jews at its peak. Only 90 people escaped the ghetto's 1944 destruction, though about 2,500 Kaunas Jews survived in German camps and 500 more joined the partisans or were saved by Lithuanians. This cemetery was destroyed in 1963, following the 1950 Soviet closure of all Jewish community institutions in Kaunas.
